title: Gai Thod – Thai Fried Chicken
description: Gai Thod is a beloved Thai-style fried chicken featuring deeply marinated, crispy chicken infused with garlic, coriander root, and white pepper. Known for its fragrant crust and juicy interior, this street-food favorite is traditionally served with sticky rice and spicy Nam Jim Jaew dipping sauce for a perfect balance of savory, sweet, spicy, and tangy flavors.

ingredients.title: For the Chicken Marinade
items: Chicken drumsticks or mid-joint wings – 1 kg, skin-on and bone-in preferred
Coriander root or stems – 2 tbsp, finely pounded
Palm sugar or regular sugar – 1 tsp

ingredients.title: For the Crispy Coating
items: Rice flour – 1 cup (for a light, crisp crust)
Tapioca flour – ¼ cup (for extra crunch)
Tempura flour – 2 tbsp (optional, for added crispness)

ingredients.title: For Fried Aromatics
items: Thai shallots – ½ cup, thinly sliced

ingredients.title: For Nam Jim Jaew Dipping Sauce (Optional)

instruction.title: Step 1 – Marinating the Chicken
steps: Pound garlic, coriander root, and white peppercorns into a fragrant Thai-style marinade paste.
Mix the paste with fish sauce, light soy sauce, oyster sauce, sugar, and salt.
Coat the chicken pieces thoroughly, cover, and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or preferably overnight for deeper flavor.

instruction.title: Step 2 – Preparing the Coating
steps: Combine rice flour, tapioca flour, tempura flour, baking powder, white pepper, and salt in a large bowl.
Coat the marinated chicken lightly with the flour mixture just before frying.
Shake off excess flour to keep the crust crisp and delicate.

instruction.title: Step 3 – Frying the Aromatics
steps: Heat neutral oil in a wok or deep pot to 160–170°C (320–340°F).
Fry sliced garlic and shallots until golden and crispy.
Remove and drain well. Reserve the fried aromatics for topping.

instruction.title: Step 4 – Frying the Chicken
steps: Increase the oil temperature slightly to 170–175°C (340–350°F).
Fry chicken in batches, turning occasionally, until golden brown and fully cooked through, about 12–15 minutes depending on size.
Transfer chicken to a wire rack and allow it to rest to maintain maximum crispness.

instruction.title: Step 5 – Serving the Gai Thod
steps: Top the fried chicken with crispy garlic and shallots.
Serve with sticky rice and Nam Jim Jaew dipping sauce.
Garnish with cucumber slices and fresh herbs for a restaurant-style presentation.

servingSuggestions.title: Serving Suggestions
items: Serve traditionally with Thai sticky rice (khao neow) and a spicy Nam Jim Jaew dipping sauce.
Pair with Som Tum (Thai green papaya salad) for a classic Thai street-food combination.
Present on a banana leaf with fresh herbs and cucumber slices for an authentic dining experience.

chefTips: For maximum crunch, try double frying: cook once at 160°C, rest briefly, then fry again at 180°C before serving.
The ideal marinade should have a balance of garlic fragrance, white pepper warmth, salty fish sauce, and subtle sweetness.
Avoid overcrowding the fryer or wok, as temperature drops will make the chicken greasy instead of crisp.
Rest fried chicken on a rack rather than paper towels to preserve the crispy coating.
Bone-in, skin-on chicken provides the juiciest texture and deeper flavor.
